subtype: Approach: checking the emergency fund first [Thinking]
passage:
I'm Francis. When the crash headlines came, I opened the investing page and my finger hovered over the button. Then I remembered Joseph.
Joseph was laid off last winter, in the middle of a fall, and had to sell his units at a bad price just to pay rent. He told me over tea that the loss was not the market's fault. It was that his cushion had been too thin.
So before doing anything, I sat with a notebook. My monthly costs come to 40,000, so six months is 2,40,000. I checked the balance in my savings accounts: 2,55,000, safe and easy to reach. I felt the knot in my chest ease.
Only after that did I look at the investing page again.
— Francis

qa.q: How much did Francis's savings accounts hold?
What was Francis feeling before checking the balance?
qa.a: Francis was uneasy and hesitant, hovering over the button, and felt relief when the balance covered six months.

qa.q: What could Francis do if the balance had been lower than six months of costs?
qa.a: Francis could build the cushion first with a monthly saving and delay any new investment until it was there.

qa.q: What might Joseph want others to learn from what happened?
qa.a: Joseph may want others to see that a thin cushion forced a sale in a fall, which is why the story stuck with Francis.

grounding: The reflection shows a person confirming six months of expenses in safe accounts before an investment decision, so that a job loss would not force a sale at a loss.
